title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas, while operating in self-driving mode with a human safety operator aboard. The vehicle did not slow down or stop after the collision. This shows a failure in the system's object detection or response logic, where a moving animal in the vehicle's path was not recognized or acted upon as an obstacle requiring evasion or braking.

The failure occurred during active deployment on public streets. A human safety operator was present but did not intervene, suggesting either that the operator did not perceive the hazard in time or that the vehicle's behavior fell within acceptable parameters in the operator's judgment. Catching this would have required either better animal detection in the autonomous system's training or a safety operator alert system that flags potential collisions before they occur.

Whether the vehicle also failed to stop at a stop sign at the location, as one resident claimed, is disputed and not established by the reports.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, generating significant community backlash. The self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, hit the duck without slowing down or stopping afterward. The incident drew additional attention because residents were familiar with this particular duck, which had been nesting near a local Italian restaurant, and they have since rescued its eggs and placed them in an incubator.

Following the accident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was in autonomous mode and investigated the incident by replaying the scene multiple times in simulation. While a resident claimed the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, Avride disputed this claim after reviewing vehicle data. The company has now adjusted its testing area by excluding certain streets around the lake and is evaluating technology improvements through controlled experiments to prevent similar situations in the future, while ensuring changes do not compromise safety performance.
